note:
Retrieval WITH the dense lane (E7). Same 200 queries, same world, same shared scorer as
retrieval-core; the only variable is that semanticScores comes from the committed
embedding fixture, keyed by evidence-store fact id.

THE PARETO POINT, AND IT WAS SWEPT RATHER THAN CHOSEN:
               recall@8  category  superseded  noise  honesty
  lexical        0.7560    0.4688      0.6000     16   0.7188
  margin 0.11    0.8393    0.6562      0.8000     34   0.6562
  margin 0.15    0.7976    0.5938      0.7000     16   0.7188   <- shipped
  margin 0.20    0.7738    0.5312      0.7000     16   0.7188
  margin 0.25    0.7560    0.4688      0.7000     16   0.7188

At 0.15 noise_lines and unknown_honesty are UNCHANGED from the lexical floor while
recall@8 gains 4.2 points and recall_category 12.5 — the metric that has been worst on
every lane since it was first measured. Nothing was bought with noise.

0.11 gains more and pays 18 noise lines and 6 points of honesty for it. That is a real
trade and deliberately NOT made inside a constant; it is recorded here so it can be taken
on purpose if the product wants it.

WHY DENSE MUST NOT DECIDE ALONE. Absolute cosine cannot separate answerable from
unanswerable: top-cosine runs 0.570-0.939 for answerable queries and 0.461-0.767 for the
32 silence-expecting ones. Admitting on it cost noise_lines 16 -> 138 and unknown_honesty
0.7188 -> 0.1875. The MARGIN does separate — top cosine minus corpus median, answerable
p10 0.092 against silence p90 0.105 — because 'I have nothing for this' looks like every
fact being equally unrelated. Dense proposes; factAffinity disposes.

NO RUN-TO-RUN VARIANCE. The vectors are committed static data replayed identically every
run, unlike the E6 shadow harness where two runs of the same pinned model differed by 16
points.

THIS IS NOT WHAT SHIPS. Production supplies no semanticScores, so retrieval-core.v1
remains the description of the live path. Wiring is E7/PR-4.

Regenerate with: npm run eval:gate -- retrieval-dense --update
